elaine_k: Quick note — onboarding sample for Java SDK changed default OkHttp timeouts and now some tests on Android 12 emulator hit READ_TIMEOUT during long polling. Repro in sampleapp polling loop attached.

peter_s: which defaults changed?

elaine_k: we switched client builder to 10s read timeout (was 60s) to reduce idle threads. That broke the polling integration tests that expect ~45s responses. Logs: 

elaine_k: 2026-04-10 10:10:01 D/OkHttp: --> GET /v1/stream/poll
elaine_k: 2026-04-10 10:10:11 E/OkHttp: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout

peter_s: Ouch. Why was it set to 10s? I thought mobile defaults were conservative.

sam_k: We changed it to 10s to avoid many idle sockets on low-tier devices, but forgot to document impact on long-poll APIs. For suspend CallAdapter v2, coroutine timeouts + OkHttp read timeout interact — coroutine may wait longer while OkHttp throws earlier. Two options: 1) document that SDK builder default keeps readTimeout=60s for long-poll endpoints, or 2) detect polling endpoints and set a higher read timeout via route-specific client.

elaine_k: For quick fix I'm reverting builder default to 60s and adding a comment in onboarding. Longer-term we should expose per-route timeout config and example code in sampleapp. I'll open PR.

devex-bot: Created ticket RED-DEVEX-4120: "Revert SDK OkHttp default readTimeout and add per-route timeout examples in sampleapp" <https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-DEVEX-4120>

peter_s: can you also add a short blurb explaining the difference between coroutine deadline vs OkHttp read timeout? Saved me yesterday.

elaine_k: will do. Thanks :thumbsup:
